messages:
claire: quick share — ran a prod-canary profiling sweep for the continuous-batcher. seeing a pattern: decode-rate oscillation causes kernel flip/flop + KV cache thrash. short prompts (<=32) with medium decode-rate (~15-35 tok/s) get classified into the fast-kernel temporarily, then evict KV entries for the longer sessions that follow -> p95 latency spikes. attaching quick config idea below.

omar: ugh. numbers? how bad is the hit-rate drop and latency bump?

claire: KV hit-rate (mixed traffic) dropped from ~92% -> ~78% during oscillation windows. p95 gen latency +50ms on affected hosts. CPU stays ok; GPU stalls visible in perf logs. sample log: 
```
[2026-02-18T15:02:04Z] host-12 decode-rate-change: 28->12 tok/s, kernel switch fast->slow, kv-evict triggered, p95 +48ms
```

jin: nice find. couple ideas: 1) add an "oscillating-decode" bucket that groups mid-rate churners and pins them behind a higher token_budget_floor so they don't cause immediate kernel switches. 2) hysteresis on kernel selection (ms) to avoid flip/flop. 3) prefix-aware KV prefetch (if session has >X prefix tokens, keep cache).

priya: memory/caching concern: if we raise token_budget_floor we could OOM smaller dedicated nodes. we should make the floor dynamic by instance type / model. maybe percent-of-host-memory cap.

alex: for rollout: recommend canary config name `osc-decode-v1` targeted to 5 hosts in us-west, run 24h, compare KV hit-rate + p95 vs baseline. if stable, scale to 20% traffic. also include regression guard: if p99 increases >100ms abort.

claire: config sketch (for batcher config): 
```json
{
  "prompt_len_bins": [0, 32, 128, 512],
  "decode_rate_buckets": ["low:<10","mid:10-40","high:>40","osc:15-35"],
  "token_budget_targets": {
    "low": 8,
    "mid": 24,
    "high": 8,
    "osc": 32
  },
  "kernel_switch_hysteresis_ms": 350,
  "kv_prefetch_prefix_tokens": 64,
  "kv_memory_fraction_cap": 0.12
}
```

omar: can we get a quick sim on trace-replay before canary? last time kernel hysteresis introduced regressions for long-running streams.

jin: yes — I'll run trace-replay. plan: baseline replay + osc-decode-v1. will output per-host KV hit-rate / kernel-switch-count / p95.

perf-bot: experiment queued by jin. replay job id: replay-20260218-420. expected runtime ~2h. emits metrics to `perf/osc-decode` index.

claire: next steps: jin runs replay and posts results, alex prepares canary rollout plan + abort criteria, priya to confirm per-instance memory cap mapping, omar to watch alerting config (p99 guard). aiming for canary by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

alex: ack, I’ll draft rollout steps in the doc and link here once ready. :party:

omar: thanks — will update on alert thresholds after checking current noise.

jin: starting the replay now. small Q: should we include kernel-selection logs in the replay trace? makes root-cause easier.

claire: yes include `kernel_name` and `kv_event` fields. thanks all.
